arxiv-1603-04644.title: Lipid membrane-mediated attraction between curvature inducing objects
arxiv-1603-04644.creator: Casper van der Wel, Afshin Vahid, Anđela Šarić, Timon Idema, Doris Heinrich, Daniela J. Kraft
arxiv-1603-04644.description: Abstract The interplay of membrane proteins is vital for many biological processes, such as cellular transport, cell division, and signal transduction between nerve cells. Theoretical considerations have led to the idea that the membrane itself mediates protein self-organization in these processes through minimization of membrane curvature energy.

arxiv-2111-15515.title: Two-pion exchange as a leading-order contribution in chiral effective field theory
arxiv-2111-15515.creator: Chinmay Mishra, A. Ekström, G. Hagen, T. Papenbrock, L. Platter
arxiv-2111-15515.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chinmay Mishra, A. Ekström, G. Hagen, T. Papenbrock, L. Platter. Pion exchange is the central ingredient to nucleon-nucleon interactions used in nuclear structure calculations, and one pion exchange (OPE) enters at leading order in chiral effective field theory. In the L J 2 ​ S + 1 = S 0 1 {}^{2S+1}L_{J}={{}^{1}S_{0}} partial wave, however, OPE and a contact term needed for proper renormalization fail to produce the qualitative, and quantitative, features of the scattering phase shifts.

arxiv-2202-10641.title: Viscous-inertial transition in dense granular suspension
arxiv-2202-10641.creator: Franco Tapia, Mie Ichihara, Olivier Pouliquen, Élisabeth Guazzelli
arxiv-2202-10641.description: Abstract Granular suspensions present a transition from a Newtonian rheology in the Stokes limit to a Bagnoldian rheology when inertia is increased. A custom rheometer which can be run in a pressure- or a volume-imposed mode is used to examine this transition in the dense regime close to jamming.

arxiv-2206-07977.title: Personalized Federated Learning via Variational Bayesian Inference
arxiv-2206-07977.creator: Xu Zhang, Yinchuan Li, Wenpeng Li, Kaiyang Guo, Yunfeng Shao
arxiv-2206-07977.description: Abstract Federated learning faces huge challenges from model overfitting due to the lack of data and statistical diversity among clients. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel personalized federated learning method via Bayesian variational inference named pFedBayes. To alleviate the overfitting, weight uncertainty is introduced to neural networks for clients and the server.

arxiv-2208-05388.title: ATLAS: Universal Function Approximator for Memory Retention
arxiv-2208-05388.creator: Heinrich P. van Deventer, Anna S. Bosman
arxiv-2208-05388.description: Abstract Artificial neural networks (ANNs), despite their universal function approximation capability and practical success, are subject to catastrophic forgetting. Catastrophic forgetting refers to the abrupt unlearning of a previous task when a new task is learned. It is an emergent phenomenon that hinders continual learning.

arxiv-2305-08743.creator: Z. Hawkhead, T. J. Hicken, N. P. Bentley, B. M. Huddart, S. J. Clark, T. Lancaster

arxiv-2504-21499.title: On L α L^{\alpha} -flatness of Erdős-Littlewood’s polynomials.
arxiv-2504-21499.creator: el Houcein el Abdalaoui ⋆
arxiv-2504-21499.description: Abstract . It is shown that Erdős-Littlewood’s polynomials are not L α L^{\alpha} -flat when α > 2 \alpha>2 is an even integer (and hence for any α ≥ 4 \alpha\geq 4 ). This provides a partial solution to an old problem posed by Littlewood.

arxiv-2505-17891.title: DAG-based Consensus with Asymmetric Trust (Extended Version)
arxiv-2505-17891.creator: Ignacio Amores-Sesar, Christian Cachin, Juan Villacis, Luca Zanolini
arxiv-2505-17891.description: Abstract . In protocols with asymmetric trust, each participant is free to make its own individual trust assumptions about others, captured by an asymmetric quorum system. This contrasts with ordinary, symmetric quorum systems and with threshold models, where all participants share the same trust assumption.
